_comment: Notification-hook surface: every priority critical|high entry whose last_changed_at falls in the last 7 days, most recently changed first. last_changed_at = max(discovered_at, every non-internal updates[].at): it moves on a new finding AND on every reader-facing update, correction or improvement (updated_at moves only on a type:update record). Poll this file and alert on a new `id` OR a changed `last_changed_at` for a known id. `immediate_action` is non-null exactly when priority is critical. URLs are absolute (`url` == `permalink`; `markdown_url` is the entry's raw Markdown source). Schema: {id, url, permalink, markdown_url, priority, kind, headline, summary, discovered_at, updated_at|null, last_changed_at, updates[{at,type,summary}], immediate_action:{title,action}|null, actions[], exploited, kev, cve_ids[], cves[{id,cvss|null,status[],affected|null,fixed|null}], affected_products[], entities[], techniques[], tags[], sectors[], regions[], verification, classification|null, org_triage:{category,rationale}|null}. exploited = an exploitation tag or a CVE status of exploited/cisa-kev; kev = a CVE on the CISA KEV list. techniques[] carries the entry's MITRE ATT&CK ids (frontmatter + prose-derived, revoked ids resolved forward); classification is the collapsed Admiralty code (e.g. B2). For the do-now task list of every priority, poll data/actions.json. See docs/pipeline.md.

alerts.headline: N-central: 4EverAble2Shell exploited on 21+ servers, Agent2Shell adds SYSTEM on agents; disable Legacy API
alerts.summary: An independent researcher published proof-of-concept code on 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-09 for what Huntress counts as 33 critical flaws in N-able's N-central remote monitoring and management appliance, and N-able released 2026.4 Hotfix 2 (build 2026.4.1.26) on 2026-11-10 with seven CVE ids; on-premises customers must upgrade their servers, then Agents and Probes. On 2026-11-12 the researcher published a second chain, 4EverAble2Shell, that pairs an Apache Axis 1.x flaw (CVE-2026-90436) with a separate root escalation and works against Hotfix 2 when the Legacy API is turned on and reachable: Huntback reports at least 21 production servers, 19 of them on Hotfix 2, running a cryptominer, Previdian's honeypot recorded attempts at the chain, and Huntress's latest guidance is that a Hotfix 2 server with the Legacy API disabled is not exposed to it. The same disclosure includes Agent2Shell, whose chains give an unauthenticated attacker who can reach the server SYSTEM commands on managed Windows endpoints and which N-able confirms also needs the Legacy API; N-able has published indicators of compromise for customers that have not disabled it, has no fix for the new claims and plans a follow-up hotfix; the Legacy API is off by default and keeping it disabled is the stated protection.

updates.summary: N-able released N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2 (build 2026.4.1.26) on 2026-11-10 with seven CVE ids, which replaces the entry's statements that no fix, no CVE ids and no affected or fixed builds existed, and reports scanning activity associated with the public proof-of-concept code but no evidence of successful exploitation; on-premises servers must be upgraded and every Agent and Probe upgraded too.

The researcher's second exploit set, 4EverAble2Shell, chains Apache Axis CVE-2026-90436 with a root escalation, works against Hotfix 2 when the Legacy API is on and is exploited on at least 21 production servers per Huntback, with attempts recorded on Previdian's honeypot; N-able has no fix yet and says it has seen no signs of compromise.

N-able confirmed via Huntress that Agent2Shell, the researcher's other chain set that gives an unauthenticated attacker SYSTEM commands on managed Windows endpoints, also needs the non-default Legacy API, and N-able has published indicators of compromise for customers that have not disabled it; N-able still has no fix, and its earlier statement that it saw no signs of compromise predates the indicators.

actions: On every ScreenConnect instance your organisation or its IT providers run, disable the RMM+ extension immediately, verify it stays disabled and do not re-enable or reinstall it (on-premises instances by hand; ConnectWise removed it from cloud-hosted ones), review Run Command and Toolbox history and the instance audit logs for executions nobody started, including before 2026-11-11, and check managed endpoints for a second ScreenConnect client service; open no interactive session to a suspect host, use EDR live response or WinRM, because a session can trigger the toolkit to spread to the technician's workstation; update every technician host client to ScreenConnect 26.6.5 or later, because a cloud-console update does not update them.

alerts.headline: ScreenConnect SCKit: second wave hits on-prem; disable RMM+, update technician clients to 26.6.5+
alerts.summary: Huntress saw an operator use access to several cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels on 2026-11-11 to run Run Command as SYSTEM on groups of managed endpoints, installing an attacker-controlled second ScreenConnect client and the SCKit toolkit on at least 288 hosts at 48 organisations within 90 minutes; Sophos independently saw the same client deployments. Huntress later said the activity seems related to the third-party RMM+ extension, whose versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 accepted a blank access key; ConnectWise's CNA record CVE-2026-127063 (CVSS 4.0 9.3) says the extension uses a static API secret by default, names no fix and gives disabling as the mitigation, while a Huntress spokesperson says the panel-access vector is still unclear and Blackpoint calls the extensions' role unresolved. A second wave on 2026-11-13 hit 205 hosts at 41 organisations (Huntress) and appears to target on-premises instances with mitigations pending (Blackpoint); Microsoft describes a rogue client built to deliver a payload to the technician who connects, which ConnectWise says ScreenConnect clients 26.6.5 and later block.

updates.summary: ConnectWise's CNA record CVE-2026-127063 (CVSS 4.0 9.3) says the RMM+ extension uses a static API secret by default, names no fix and gives disabling as the mitigation; Huntress's spokesperson and Blackpoint leave the panel-access vector unresolved, so the explanations differ and the action now names RMM+ specifically.

Microsoft's analysis describes RelayTrap, a rogue client built on the endpoint to deliver a payload to the technician who connects, and browser-cookie routines designed to push tools through the Shared Toolbox; ConnectWise says clients 26.6.5 and later block the transfer, and a second wave on 2026-11-13 hit 205 hosts at 41 organisations, one with a self-hosted RMM+, so every technician client now belongs on the action list.

actions: Find every Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controller, and any other refrigeration controller with a remote management interface because not every second-wave site's vendor is confirmed, in facilities you own or that a contractor manages for you and take its management interface off the internet now, restoring access only through a secure VPN or protected network (filtering to the contractor's source addresses is an emergency stop-gap, and CERT-FR asks you to check your insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink); an end-of-life unit that gets no fixes needs replacing, because a factory reset leaves it vulnerable and probably compromised again.

On every such controller that was reachable from the internet, check the whole configuration, defrost ranges, alarm thresholds and notification recipients included, against the intended one, verify the actual temperatures and test that alarms reach staff; for a Danfoss unit that may have been taken over, restart it or otherwise factory-reset it, restore access only through a secure VPN or protected network and reconfigure it for service, then update its firmware, set the security level to Strict and replace the default and any weak passwords, which do not close the six unpatched AK-SM 800A flaws that Midnight Blue and CCB report, so the interface stays off the internet; change all credentials where compromise is suspected and check the devices attached to the controllers, as BSI advises; and on every Copeland or Dixell XWEB unit confirm the factory Admin password was changed and give each contractor a named account with an expiry date.
alerts.headline: Danfoss AK-SM 800A: six unpatched pre-auth RCE flaws, Strict mode does not remove them; France blames IRGC
alerts.summary: Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026, a remotely forced defrost at hundreds of French stores, and on 2026-11-09 France's foreign ministry attributed that campaign, and only that campaign, to the Iranian unit Shahid Kaveh. More followed: more than 115 stores in at least six more countries and the first German shops on 2026-11-02, altered cold-room settings at three sites of the French blood service through a supplier, and, per SRF on 2026-11-05, a Köniz butcher and three Volg stores in Switzerland. CERT-FR reports numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and of Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, and NCSC Switzerland rates the activity actively exploited. On 2026-11-11 Midnight Blue reported six pre-authentication remote-code-execution flaws in all Danfoss AK-SM 800A firmware up to 5.3.2, with no CVE identifier or fixed version and no known exploitation (BSI); CCB says updating, new passwords and Strict mode are insufficient, so removing internet exposure comes first, and BACS's statement of 2026-11-10 that updates fix the known flaws predates the report and does not cover the six.

updates.summary: CERT-FR revised its alert on 2026-10-13 to add Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb to the compromised controllers, says campaigns are probably still running, and says a factory reset alone is insufficient on an unpatched end-of-life unit. NCSC Switzerland published an advisory rating the activity actively exploited and naming the current AK-SM 800A on outdated firmware, and Danfoss says that is the case for the affected current units. Blick reports that Migros uses the same Danfoss systems in a limited number of Swiss stores and sees no sign they were targeted.

Censys's exposure report of 2026-10-14 points to three published 2025 AK-SM 800A flaws that Danfoss patched more than a year earlier and gives their firmware boundaries (4.3.1 or later fixes all three; Danfoss has not confirmed the vector), and shows exposed French controllers falling about 71 percent in three days with patched and unpatched builds leaving at the same rate, which Censys reads as operators taking units offline rather than patching.

CERT-FR's alert has a third version dated 2026-10-16 whose guidance differs for compromised and uncompromised units: the whole configuration, defrost ranges included, is to be checked, and a compromised Danfoss unit is to be restarted or otherwise factory-reset and reconfigured, with a caution to check insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink. The Dixell France operator guide that the alert links says any XWEB PRO on firmware 1.12.1 or earlier must be updated without delay, that XWEB units ship with a factory Admin account, and that remote access must go through an encrypted VPN; neither document names an entry vector.

The Dixell France guide that CERT-FR links was replaced on 2026-10-18 and now carries Copeland's own bulletin of 14 October 2026, which acknowledges the vulnerability on a discontinued, end-of-life generation of XWEB EVO controllers, says to remove every XWEB EVO from the public internet at once, gives a restore procedure and says to check product temperatures in the cabinets directly; the earlier statements about XWEB PRO firmware 1.12.1, a CISA advisory and a March 2024 bulletin are no longer on that page and are removed. Le Monde's report that the defrost operation was lengthened from one hour to eight so that alarms trigger late, and SecurityWeek's figure of about 700 supermarkets, the prosecutor's report of fires and the absence of a claim or ransom demand, are added, with Cybersecurity Dive's report that Copeland confirmed the flaw was found in discontinued controllers.

ANSSI's director general told the French Senate on 2026-10-21 that elementary flaws were exploited, starting with controllers directly on the internet, administered without particular protection, and weak passwords, not vulnerabilities researchers had published, so a firmware update alone does not close the exposure. Forescout, on 2026-10-22, counts 12,976 exposed service observations in 99 countries, 3,762 exposed Danfoss StoreView observations on AK-SM 800A units, 80 percent of the 4,697 StoreView observations, on firmware older than 4.3.1, and over 20 hacktivist-claimed refrigeration attacks since January 2026, and says the French access vector remains unconfirmed.

Reuters reports that the Pentagon treats late-August freezer failures at at least six US military commissaries as a suspected hack, with Cyber Command and Army investigators in touch with their French counterparts, and Nextgov adds that two people familiar with the matter say US officials suspect Iran-linked hackers; neither says how the intruders got in, and no official has attributed the activity on the record.

The attacks returned on 2026-11-02 across Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Sweden, Ireland and Estonia, and Finland per The Guardian: BleepingComputer counts more than 115 stores and says it is unclear whether the attacks were coordinated, Sabcobel says its sites were hit through the same vulnerability as in France, Euronews names Danfoss as the software supplier in both incidents while CyberInsider says the manufacturer and access method of the new wave remain unknown, and Coop Switzerland says attempts against it failed.

The attacks reached Germany: heise reports an Edeka market in Reisbach whose cooling systems were heated to 50 degrees overnight into 2 November, WDR quotes a CAP supermarket manager saying the attack hit the firm that maintains the cooling plants remotely and reports that Rewe's head office confirmed an attack aimed at Danfoss; SentinelLABS says responsibility has not been publicly established; and Le Canard enchaîné reports that cold rooms of a contractor of the French blood service were programmed to 110 degrees overnight on 1 to 2 November, with no source tying that case to these controllers.

The French blood service EFS confirmed that an incident at its refrigeration supplier on 2 November altered the temperature and defrost thresholds of cold rooms at three of its sites, caught by its own alarms with no loss of blood products, so the case no longer rests on Le Canard enchaîné alone; ENISA, the European Commission, Europol and the CSIRTs Network advised organisations on 2026-11-04 to take immediate action, CSIRT Italia issued cold-chain measures, and no source ties the blood-service case to the Danfoss, Copeland or Dixell controllers.

SRF reported on 2026-11-05 the first publicly known cases of the refrigeration attacks in Switzerland, a butcher in Köniz whose freezer reached 50 to 70 degrees and three Volg stores with changed cooling parameters; BACS has received one reportable notification about an attack on commercial refrigeration, and CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA and DOT published a joint fact sheet on refrigeration and cold-chain controllers that names no vendor, CVE or actor. No source names the controller make or the access route in the Swiss cases.

NCSC Switzerland updated its advisory on 2026-11-06 with the Swiss incidents, Copeland and Dixell XWEB and healthcare, a four-point checklist for refrigeration management systems across all relevant operations, supplier-managed equipment included, and the statement that the public information does not establish a common attack method or confirm exploitation of the Danfoss CVEs it lists. Ransom-ISAC published the event log of one internet-reachable Copeland XWEB Pro compromise (743 parameter writes in two administrator sessions, default credentials claimed without published evidence), and Unit 42 counts over 5,000 exposed devices across countries on 5 and 6 November and a falling count in France since October.

France's foreign ministry and the C4 crisis cell attributed the 11 to 12 October refrigeration-controller campaign to Iran on 2026-11-09, naming the Revolutionary Guard unit Shahid Kaveh, and the Paris prosecutor requested arrest warrants against its leader and two deputies; the French documents cover that campaign only, and the later waves and the Swiss cases are not attributed in them.

BACS published its own public warning on 2026-11-10: it says Switzerland is affected and that the controllers also run in butchers, restaurants, pharmacies, doctors' practices, laboratories, logistics, industry and farms, many of whose operators do not know their plants are reachable from the internet, and it repeats that security updates for the AK-SM 800A and 8xxA family exist and that newer firmware enforces HTTPS.

Midnight Blue reported on 2026-11-11 six pre-authentication remote-code-execution flaws in all Danfoss AK-SM 800A firmware up to 5.3.2, with no CVE identifier, no fixed version and no known exploitation (BSI); CCB says updating, new passwords and Strict mode are insufficient and removing internet exposure comes first, and BSI will not rule out flaws in firmware 5.4.0 (heise).

alerts.headline: NetScaler: 28 flaws fixed, one reaches every default ADC and Gateway; update to 14.1-73.57 or 13.1-64.39
alerts.summary: Cloud Software Group's bulletin CTX697305 of 2026-11-12 fixes 28 flaws in customer-managed NetScaler ADC and Gateway, 9 of them scored CVSS 4.0 9.0 or above; CVE-2026-120868 (9.3) needs no feature or authentication and affects every deployment in default configuration, and CVE-2026-107412 (9.5) reaches Gateway and AAA virtual servers. The fixed builds are 14.1-73.57, 13.1-64.39, 14.1-73.58 FIPS and 13.1-37.293, and bulletin CTX697320 fixes an unauthenticated NetScaler Console authentication bypass in 14.1-74.34; the bulletins describe the impact as unpredictable behaviour or denial of service, offer no workaround and state no exploitation status, while CERT-EU writes that Citrix reports none and no source reports an attack.

alerts.summary: Check Point Research reports that from 2026-10-30 an attacker exploited unpatched Check Point gateways through the Mobile Access portal with PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), escalated to root with CVE-2026-123039 (CVSS 7.8, a local flaw in the dynamic_server process that Check Point says was exploited against a couple of dozen customers), installed a persistent backdoor and in the first wave deleted files on a VMware ESXi host. The fix for both is in Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator R81.20 take 174, R82 take 132, R82.10 take 52 and R82.20 take 14 or later, with none listed for R81.10 or R81, and the standalone PHP hotfix is not stated to cover CVE-2026-123039; sk1000302 itself carries no statement on exploitation.

actions: Tell the helpdesk, HR and payroll teams of every body whose staff are insured with Publica (including the federal administration and the ETH domain) or with the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, which says data of its insured persons and pensioners was stolen, that AHV number, date of birth, address, salary and IBAN may now be known to criminals and must not count as proof of identity, and route requests that quote them, a request to change a payout account included, to a call-back on a known number; for staff insured with Pensionskasse Post, the Bernische Pensionskasse (which can neither confirm nor rule out that its insured persons' data left), the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT (which found data of about 1,800 of its insured persons on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more), the Pensionskasse der Stadt Zug (which reports an elevated but unconfirmed risk that its insured persons' data left), a fund administered or advised by Libera AG or the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse apply the same rule until those funds report the scope; also tell insured staff that cantonal police warn of investment-fraud calls from people who know their salary and pension details, which prove nothing about the caller.

If your organisation's pension administration, HR or payroll runs on PK Softech software, is being migrated to it or tested on it, or your staff are insured with Pensionskasse Post, ask the supplier or the fund in writing whether your data, test data included, was in the affected environment, project, test and migration copies included, and what it holds outside the productive system.
alerts.headline: PK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had promised in writing to delete; Tamedia says Akira holds about 100 GB
alerts.summary: PK Softech AG, the software supplier of Publica and other Swiss pension funds, says unknown attackers used malware to reach part of its IT and that data must be assumed to have left; the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating and has added the case to its criminal proceeding against Akira. Tamedia reports that Akira holds about 100 GB and demands ransom, while PK Softech and the federal bodies say no concrete ransom demand reached them; Publica and several other funds say their insured persons' personal data has presumably left. Cantonal police warn that criminals could use leaked personal and financial data for investment-fraud calls.

updates.summary: The supplier's customers are now named: the Bernische Pensionskasse (canton of Bern staff and three cantonal universities) says its supplier is the same company that serves Publica, the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse and Pensionskasse Post report the supplier incident, and Inside IT lists Migros-Pensionskasse and Syngenta Pensionskasse among the customers. None of the funds has confirmed which member data left.

Publica's own page of 2026-10-08 lists civil status and the IBAN among the data that could be affected and says its investigation indicates personal data of insured persons has presumably left. The AWP agency relays the software firm's position that it knows data left but not yet whether personal data is among it, that it may be business data, and that the volume is rather small.

The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, the City of Zurich's pension fund, says on 2026-10-13 that it currently uses another provider, plans to move to PK Softech's system in early 2027 and is checking whether data from migration tests was affected. Publica's page says as of 2026-10-14 that it has no indications that data from the attack was published on the darkweb.

Cantonal police warn that criminals could use the leaked salary and pension data to phone insured persons with investment-fraud offers, SwissCybersecurity.net ties the warning to PK Softech, and the Zurich cantonal fund BVK says its PK Softech software runs in its own data centre so it is not directly affected; PK Softech can neither confirm nor rule out further affected customers, and the Ticino fund listed as a customer has made no statement.

The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, the City of Zurich's pension fund, now says in its notice of 2026-10-15 that its inquiries indicate personal data of its insured persons and pensioners, handed to PK Softech as test data for a planned 2027 switch, was stolen, and that which fields were taken is still being clarified. Pensionskasse Post says in its notice of the same date that personal data did leave and no longer repeats its earlier anonymisation statement, though it is still unclear whether its insured persons' data is among it.

SonntagsBlick reports, from a confidential federal information note, that the Confederation rates the incident as serious and says the security organs of the Confederation are particularly affected, which it glosses as the Federal Intelligence Service, the Defence Group and fedpol, that the Federal Council was briefed on 2026-10-14 and that the cantons were informed; the Finance Department confirms only the briefing. NZZ adds that the pension consultancy Libera AG is also affected, that the Bernische Pensionskasse now says it must be assumed personal data left, and that Publica ran no regular on-site audits at the supplier.

Tamedia reports, and Inside IT relays, that the Akira ransomware group holds about 100 GB of the pension data of well over 100,000 current and former federal employees, with employer details of staff under cover identity among it, and demands ransom; neither the Confederation nor Publica confirms the actor or the demand.

Netzwoche, relaying Tages-Anzeiger, reports that the Federal Council and the security authorities now assume data on practically all current and former federal and federally affiliated staff left, federal judges and former Federal Council members among them, and that an on-site inspection at PK Softech on 2026-10-07 established the outflow of security-relevant data; neither the Confederation nor Publica has confirmed the actor, the demand or the scope.

The supplier's written pledge to delete Publica's 2019 migration data was apparently not kept, Inside IT relays that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira exfiltrated data, though that is second-hand and neither the Confederation nor Publica has itself named the actor, and the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says all its insured could potentially be involved but has no evidence yet that data was taken.

The Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says in a letter of 2026-10-23 that data of about 1,800 of its insured persons (about 1,700 who left in 2024 and 2025, with exit-benefit amounts and IBANs, and about 80 on disability pensions) sat on the attacked supplier server for two ongoing projects; it has no certain evidence the data were taken but finds it plausible, and it writes to all insured because it cannot exclude more.

The Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (EDÖB) opened a formal investigation against PK Softech on 2026-10-22, after an informal inquiry at Publica on 2026-10-14, and states that data of several pension funds, Publica among them, was exfiltrated; the investigation is to establish which personal data the funds handed to the supplier, on what legal basis, and how much left.

The entry said that neither the Confederation nor Publica had named the actor. Publica's own newsletter of 2026-10-22 says the Akira group is being associated with the attack, and that Publica filed a criminal complaint with the Federal Prosecutor's Office on 2026-10-15; the summary, the sourcing note and the paragraph on the Akira reporting now say so, a population figure was trimmed from the analysis, and the demand and the Prosecutor's Office confirmation still rest on press reports.

The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich suspended its planned 2027 move to PK Softech's administration system; PK Softech, quoted by watson.ch, cannot rule out that non-pseudonymised data was temporarily present in project work, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office has added the case to its criminal proceeding against the Akira group.

The Bernische Pensionskasse's own notices say it does not know, and can neither confirm nor rule out, whether its insured persons' data left, and it assumes only that more data left the supplier than first thought, while the NZZ quoted it more broadly; its letter also says ransomware was installed at the supplier on 2026-09-29, and watson.ch found no PK Softech entry on Akira's leak site a month after the attack. Inside IT names the supplier's customers in its own voice, citing AWP only for PK Softech's statement, and the September 2025 deletion request is Publica's statement to watson.ch.

The Pensionskasse der Stadt Zug, whose administrator Libera AG uses PK Softech software, said on 2026-11-09 that there is an elevated, not yet confirmed risk that its insured persons' data left the supplier, and has informed its insured persons and the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner.

PK Softech and the State Secretariat for Security Policy said on 2026-11-10 that no concrete ransom demand reached the supplier or the federal bodies, that the supplier never contacted the attackers, that the Confederation paid nothing and that there is still no indication of publication on the darkweb, which qualifies the press report that Akira demands ransom.

Publica's own page of 2026-11-10 says the supplier received general extortion letters immediately after the attack, never made concrete with an amount or payment deadline, while PK Softech's page names no letter; watson.ch reports that PK Softech ignores the negotiation-chat prompt Akira left in its network, and SRF's report of a concrete demand with a threat to publish remains unconfirmed by the supplier, Publica and the federal bodies.

alerts.headline: Node-RED flaw in Siemens IoT2050 hit a VulnCheck canary; V4.3.4-1 fixes Industrial OS, Example Image has no fix
alerts.summary: Siemens ProductCERT advisory SSA-834709 of 2026-08-11 discloses CVE-2026-58115, rated 10.0 on both CVSS 3.1 and 4.0: SIMATIC IoT2050 devices with Node-RED installed do not enforce authentication on the Node-RED HTTP interface, so an unauthenticated attacker with network reach can create a flow and run code with maximum privileges. Siemens' advisory, revised on 2026-11-10, lists the Advanced, Basic, M.2 and SM variants in two configurations: all versions below V4.3.4-1 running Industrial OS, fixed in V4.3.4-1, and all versions running Example Image versions, for which no fix is available; Siemens offers uninstalling or hardening Node-RED as interim mitigations. VulnCheck reports that on 2026-10-30 one of its canaries caught exploitation, a single request that deployed a flow downloading and running a Linux bot, with web-shell flows from the same address since; the target was a canary and the activity looks like opportunistic mass scanning.

updates.summary: VulnCheck reports that on 2026-10-30 one of its canaries caught an attacker exploiting CVE-2026-58115 with a single unauthenticated request that deployed a flow downloading and running a Linux bot, with web-shell flows from the same address since; no Siemens device is reported compromised.

Siemens revised its advisory SSA-834709 to V1.1 on 2026-11-04 and now lists the SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced, Basic, M.2 and SM variants as affected, all versions below V4.3.4-1 with Node-RED installed; the fix and interim mitigations are unchanged, so owners of the three further variants are in scope as well.

Siemens revised SSA-834709 to V1.2 on 2026-11-10 and added a second affected configuration for each of the four IoT2050 variants, all versions running Example Image versions with Node-RED installed, for which no fix is available; the V4.3.4-1 fix and the interim mitigations apply only as stated for Industrial OS and Node-RED.

alerts.headline: Certighost AD CS flaw: Kaspersky sees a ransomware group attempting the public exploit; patch every Enterprise CA
alerts.summary: Researchers published exploitation details and a public PoC (2026-07-24) for "Certighost" (CVE-2026-54121), an Active Directory Certificate Services flaw Microsoft patched on 2026-07-14: a low-privileged domain user can make an Enterprise CA issue a certificate carrying a Domain Controller's identity, authenticate as that DC via PKINIT, and DCSync the krbtgt hash. alerts.headline: Barracuda ESG: CISA lists both flaws as exploited, Barracuda reports attacks; update to 9.4.0.029 or later
alerts.summary: Barracuda's advisory of 2026-11-02 covers CVE-2026-116606, a pre-authentication authorization bypass in the Email Security Gateway (CVSS 9.3) that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker restore a crafted backup archive through the configuration-import function, and CVE-2026-111560, a command injection in the timezone field (8.6) that also affects the Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, Web Application Firewall and Web Security Gateway; chained, they give root. watchTowr Labs showed on 2026-11-05 that the chain needs no account, one unauthenticated request to the login handler reaching the restore function, and Barracuda changed its advisory the same day to say authentication is not required for CVE-2026-116606, only that the administrative interface must be reachable; watchTowr published a detection tool. Barracuda added on 2026-11-09 that it has identified exploitation activity affecting a small number of organizations, without naming the flaw, the Canadian Cyber Centre says open-source reporting indicates CVE-2026-116606 is exploited in the wild, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-10 and marks both for forensic triage. Barracuda names firmware 9.4.0.029 as the fixed build while the CVE record lists builds before 9.4.0.030 as affected.

updates.summary: watchTowr Labs published the full chain on 2026-11-05 and a detection tool: one unauthenticated request to the Email Security Gateway's login handler reaches the backup-restore function, a secret that is hard-coded in the product lets an attacker build a valid archive, and the restored timezone value reaches the root command injection, so exploitation needs no account; Barracuda changed its own advisory the same day to say authentication is not required for CVE-2026-116606. No source reports attacks.

Barracuda's advisory now says it has identified exploitation activity affecting a small number of organizations without naming the flaw, and the Canadian Cyber Centre says open-source reporting indicates CVE-2026-116606 is exploited in the wild, so the earlier statement that no source reports attacks no longer holds.

CISA added both Barracuda flaws, CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-10, so the exploitation Barracuda reported without naming a flaw is now tied to both and CVE-2026-111560 moves to exploited; CISA marks both for forensic triage.

alerts.summary: Huntress observed from 2026-10-07 23:20 UTC attackers chaining two AhsayCBS flaws, CVE-2026-105133 (authentication bypass) and CVE-2026-105134 (code execution as SYSTEM through the Replication Receiver API), against internet-exposed servers of the backup management console that managed service providers and system integrators mainly use, dropping JSP webshells and an XMRig cryptominer; Bitdefender MDR investigated three intrusions through the same chain, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-14. Ahsay now says its earlier patches v9.15.2.59 and v10.3.4.0 did not fully address the flaws, so servers on them are still exposed; the fixes are the hotfixes v10.3.4.45 (v10) and v9.15.2.70 (v7, v8 and v9), available only to partners with a portal login, and a server that was reachable before the hotfix needs a compromise check.

updates.summary: Ahsay says its previous patches v9.15.2.59 and v10.3.4.0 did not fully fix the flaws and names the hotfixes v10.3.4.45 and v9.15.2.70, available only to partners; Huntress verified the v10 hotfix, CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-14, and Bitdefender MDR describes three intrusions through the chain. Hotfixes now cover v10 and v7 to v9, through the partner portal.

Horizon3.ai's source-level analysis of 2026-10-14 gives the root cause of both flaws (a caller-set flag that skips the administrator credential check, and an upload path that escapes the folder denylist), shows the chain runs as root on Linux, and lists server-side hunt artifacts: new .jsp files in served application directories, replication receivers created outside a change window, unexpected system administrator accounts, and requests carrying the bypass field or the receiver upload headers.

Huntress's follow-up on servers exploited between 8 and 11 October, before the hotfixes, describes five webshell families, a second miner and a host-bound Python implant, plus Veeam credential theft on a neighbouring server; it advises a full re-image from a trusted backup and rotation of the credentials the server held or could reach.

alerts.headline: Balbooa Gridbox for Joomla: anonymous Super User flaws exploited since July; update to 2.20.5.0
alerts.summary: The mySites.guru research campaign against Joomla third-party extensions produced six further disclosures between 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-23, and one of them changes technique class: the Balbooa Gridbox page builder (CVE-2026-61425) trusts a client-supplied cookie value as proof of identity, so setting an administrator's username in that cookie authenticates the requester as that user with no password and no existing session. A Joomla Super User can edit templates, which is PHP execution, so this is full site compromise from a single anonymous request. Fixed in Gridbox 2.20.1; the researcher says the vulnerable code shipped for at least nine months. The same week added unauthenticated SQL injection and order-forgery flaws in EasyStore, an invoice IDOR in Events Booking, and a critical unauthenticated upload in Membership Pro. A follow-up audit of Gridbox produced eleven more CVEs, fixed in 2.20.2, four of them exploited in the wild, and Gridbox 2.20.3.1 (21 September) fixes a further unauthenticated SQL injection present in every earlier build. Gridbox 2.20.4.2 (27 October) fixes two more unauthenticated SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 and CVE-2026-102789, with no exploitation reported, and Gridbox version 2.20.5.0 (4 November) fixes four more flaws, the worst an unauthenticated file deletion, also with no exploitation reported.

updates.summary: A follow-on source-code audit of the Balbooa Gridbox page builder for Joomla, commissioned by the vendor after an earlier authentication-bypass disclosure, found 23 further vulnerabilities in the single component. Two now carry CVEs: CVE-2026-65884 (CVSS 4.0 10.0) because the registration handler adds the usergroup IDs a visitor asks for instead of replacing them, letting an anonymous user create an administrator account outright, and CVE-2026-65885 (CVSS 4.0 9.4), an authenticated arbitrary file upload that turns the first into end-to-end unauthenticated remote code execution. The Joomla CNA marks both as attacked, and the researcher reports server-log evidence of exploitation plus 92 planted administrator accounts on one connected site. Every release from 1.0.0 to 2.20.1 is affected; the complete fix is Gridbox 2.20.2.

All eleven Joomla CNA records for the Gridbox 2.20.2 batch have now published. Seven are Critical, and four carry the exploit maturity Attacked: besides CVE-2026-65884 and CVE-2026-65885, already recorded here, CVE-2026-65887 resets the password of any account except Super Users and CVE-2026-65888 logs the caller in as any user through the social login method, both CVSS 4.0 10.0. Both are added. Balbooa has since shipped 2.20.2.3, a hardening release with no CVE, and 2.20.3.1, which fixes an unauthenticated blind SQL injection in the blog author parameter present in every earlier build, so the action now points at 2.20.3.1. The sourcing note reflects the exploitation now recorded and which parts rest on one source. The mySites.guru quotation follows the round-up's current text and names the page it comes from, and one phrase about how the coverage was produced is reworded. The summary mentions the follow-up releases, and verification is recorded as multi-source now that the vendor's release notes are among the sources.

Balbooa released Gridbox 2.20.4.2 on 2026-10-27, fixing two unauthenticated read-side SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 (the sort-by parameter of store and category post lists) and CVE-2026-102789 (an editor task without a permission check), both scored CVSS 4.0 9.3 by the Joomla CNA and affecting every release up to 2.20.4.1. No exploitation is reported, Joomla 3 sites have no fix, and the action now points at 2.20.4.2.

The analysis no longer says there is no exploitation signal or that the cookie name is withheld; the October 2025 release is treated as a lower bound on exposure, not its start; the CVE record's 9.4 score beside the discloser's 10.0, Membership Pro's CVSS 3.1 rating and its default-configuration impact, Balbooa's wording on web-server rules and the attribution of the read-side reading are corrected; the headline is current.

Balbooa released Gridbox version 2.20.5.0 on 2026-11-04 with four more security fixes, the worst an unauthenticated deletion of files by path, so 2.20.5.0 replaces 2.20.4.2 as the build to install; no source reports exploitation of the four.

alerts.headline: CISA lists WordPress core's upgrade-window RCE race as exploited; block wp-content/upgrade before installing 7.1.4
alerts.summary: WordPress 7.1.4 of 2026-10-28 fixes a weakness in the core upgrade process that lets an unauthenticated attacker reach the staged installer and run code on the server during a full-package core update, in versions 4.7 to 7.1.3, with backports for every branch down to 4.7. CISA added CVE-2026-119977 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-03; Wordfence reports more than 18,500 probing requests in the first 21 hours, while Patchstack calls the race hard to win and says it needs a web-reachable staging directory. The discoverer says the update that installs the fix still unpacks with the old code, so the staging directory must be blocked before updating.

updates.summary: Wordfence assigned CVE-2026-119977 (CVSS 3.1 8.1) to the WordPress upgrade-window race after the entry was written; the statements that no CVE identifier exists are replaced and the CVE record is added.

CISA added CVE-2026-119977 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-03 on evidence of active exploitation, so the flaw is now listed as exploited; the catalog entry names no victim or method, and Wordfence's probing telemetry remains the only described activity.

The discoverer, Umut Bayram of Picus Security, shows that the update installing WordPress 7.1.4 still unpacks with the site's old code, so the staging folder under wp-content/upgrade can be reachable at a predictable path during that update, while a partial package exposes the installer only if it contains the installer files; he advises denying web access to the folder and confirming it answers 403 before updating.
The wp-config.php check follows Picus's account of the attack, which copies a malicious configuration over the live one and can point the site at an attacker-controlled database.

actions: In every Entra tenant you run or manage for others, list the app registrations that hold client secrets, starting with multitenant, delegated-admin (GDAP) and Partner Center apps, security-tool integration apps and Azure DevOps service connections, and search the service-principal and non-interactive sign-in logs for the invalid-secret or expired-secret errors AADSTS7000215 and AADSTS7000222 followed by a success for the same app; on any hit remove all client secrets, certificates and federated credentials on that app, including ones you did not add, disable its service principal if needed and rotate everything stored in any Key Vault it could read, because issued tokens stay valid until they expire.
alerts.headline: Entra app-credential abuse: agents hunt GitHub for secrets, an operator reaches MSP clients, government among them
alerts.summary: Microsoft reports that since August threat actors have used the agentic framework ARTEX to query public GitHub for OAuth application secrets and cloud keys, and that from 2026-10-28 valid application credentials were used for service-principal sign-ins across dozens of applications in several tenants, a vendor-owned multitenant application among them. Todyl's telemetry shows one operator since 2026-11-01 targeting about 45 application registrations at MSPs, more than 33 of which authenticated, and reaching 27 organisations, government clients among them; Microsoft says a similar campaign involving the same addresses was reported by Todyl, and Todyl's update of 2026-11-06 now assesses its operator as an automated agentic credential crawler, likely fed by secrets exposed in public repositories or web apps.

updates.summary: Todyl updated its investigation on 2026-11-06: it now assesses its operator as an automated agentic credential crawler, accepts Microsoft's ARTEX naming and GitHub access path, and names AI agents writing secrets in cleartext on the command line as the largest source of exposed credentials it has seen.

alerts.headline: Node2Shell Brotli flaw is now on CISA KEV, with exploit traffic seen against Node.js 24.22.0; update now
alerts.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation, and ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26, though its own copy of the attacker's chain got no shell. Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 fix it, and because the flaw is in Google's decoder the PyPI packages Brotli (1.2.1) and brotlicffi (1.2.1.0), Envoy, Microsoft .NET, PHP for Windows, Ubuntu and, with Brotli inspection and TLS decryption enabled, PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls carry it too; Palo Alto and Cisco report no malicious use against their own products. Broadcom lists VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager 9.1.1.x as critically affected (CVSS 3.1 9.8), with the patch pending and only workarounds available, and Splunk lists Splunk Enterprise 10.0 (not 9.4, and not 10.2 or later) among the products that include affected Node.js packages, with 10.2 or later as the upgrade target and its Visual Exporter app, present in every version, to be disabled.

updates.summary: Envoy and Microsoft have shipped fixes for the same Brotli decoder flaw: Envoy's advisory of 2026-10-23 lists v1.40.0, v1.39.3, v1.38.6, v1.37.8 and v1.36.12 for deployments with the Brotli decompressor configured, and Microsoft's out-of-band .NET release of 2026-10-25 (8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14) covers applications that decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data. Still no source reports exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory demonstration.

NCSC Switzerland rates exploitation of the Brotli flaw unknown with a proof of concept available and names rejecting Content-Encoding: br as the interim measure; Palo Alto lists PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls that inspect Brotli traffic with TLS decryption enabled (hotfixes due by 2026-10-30), and PHP for Windows and Ubuntu shipped fixes. Still no source reports exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory demonstration.

CISA added CVE-2026-111497 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation, and ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26; JFrog shows the decoder reachable beyond HTTP and Cisco and Palo Alto report no malicious use against their products. The entry's earlier statement that no source reports exploitation is replaced, the priority moves from notable to high. Palo Alto's advisory, as read on 2026-10-28, shows six of its nine PAN-OS hotfixes released and three due on 2026-10-29 and 2026-10-30.

Broadcom's advisory VMSA-2026-0008.1 lists VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager as affected, critical (CVSS 3.1 9.8) on 9.1.1 and important (7.5) on 9.1.0, 9.0.x and 5.2.x, with the patch pending and workarounds only; the SDDC Manager workaround is added to the actions. Palo Alto's timeline of 2026-10-29 records the last three PAN-OS hotfixes (11.2.4-h23, 12.1.4-h13 and 12.1.10-h3) as released, so the PAN-OS action no longer says they are due. Removed from the main text: ELLIO's reading of the attacker as a mass-exploitation operator and its count of 50 attempts (the 2026-10-28 section still carries them). The Ubuntu 20.04 entry in the CVE record now shows the ESM fix.

An earlier section's statement that no source reported exploitation outside the laboratory is dated to the day it held; NCSC Switzerland now rates the flaw actively exploited, and Zscaler's first-day decoy telemetry joins ELLIO's. Datadog's detection layers (decoder errors, worker crashes, leaked decompressed output) and what does not catch the attack are added, as is Palo Alto's Prisma Cloud Transporter Client.

Patchstack reports that default WordPress installs reach the Brotli decoder without authentication through the xmlrpc.php pingback and the operating system's libbrotli, shown to crash a worker but not to execute code; WordPress hosts need a patched libbrotli package, which the official WordPress image did not yet carry.

Splunk's advisory lists Splunk Enterprise 10.0 and lower, its Visual Exporter app, SOAR Automation Broker, UBA and Attack Analyzer as including packages affected by four Node.js flaws, CVE-2026-111497 among them, with Splunk Enterprise 10.2 or higher as the upgrade target and the Visual Exporter app to be disabled, and Citrix names Unicon eLux Scout with hotfix 2609.1, 2508 CU2 LTSR and 2605.1-3 as the fixes.

Splunk narrowed advisory SVD-2026-1015 on 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-06: only Splunk Enterprise 10.0 is vulnerable, 9.4 and 10.2 or later are not, so the upgrade applies to 10.0 instances alone while the Visual Exporter app is still to be disabled on every version. The revision adds Splunk Observability components and a Synthetic Runner fix, Keycloak 26.8.2 fixes the flaw in its bundled Brotli decoder, and the 27 October statement that no source reported exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory was outdated, since ELLIO had reported exploit traffic on 26 October.
